renders._yaml:
- component: figure title: Family trees description: |- Each tree is a protein family: branches are drawn from the root with their length in substitutions per site, and each dot is a member at the tip of a branch. It answers how the members of a family relate to each other. How to read: members on short branches close together are near-identical, and long branches mark divergent members. A family filter draws one tree. Hover a dot to read the member and its family. Lines and annotations: the horizontal scale is the branch length from the root, estimated by CMAPLE. No support values or cut-offs are drawn. code: |- d = df.sort('draw_order') traces = [] for fam in d['family'].unique(maintain_order=True).to_list(): part = d.filter(pl.col('family') == fam) tips = part.filter(pl.col('is_tip')) traces.append(go.Scatter( x=part['x'].to_list(), y=part['y'].to_list(), mode='lines', connectgaps=False, line={'width': 1}, hoverinfo='skip', showlegend=False, legendgroup=fam, )) traces.append(go.Scatter( x=tips['x'].to_list(), y=tips['y'].to_list(), mode='markers', marker={'size': 6}, text=tips['node'].to_list(), customdata=tips['family'].to_list(), hovertemplate='%{text}
%{customdata}', showlegend=False, legendgroup=fam, )) fig = go.Figure(data=traces) fig.update_layout(xaxis_title='Substitutions per site from the root', margin={'t': 16, 'l': 16, 'r': 16, 'b': 48}) fig.update_yaxes(visible=False, autorange='reversed')

- component: table
  title: Tree segments
  description: |-
    Each row is a point of a tree drawing: its family, horizontal distance from the root, vertical slot and, at a tip, the member. It answers what the figure is drawn from.
    How to read: this is a drawing table with separator rows, so use the family filter and the figure rather than reading it row by row.
